data.title: Energy refund "processing fee" demand from Verbraucher-Rückerstattungsstelle Energie
data.case_title: Suspicious €49.90 advance-fee demand for claimed €612 energy refund
data.summary: A sender calling itself "Verbraucher-Rückerstattungsstelle Energie" based in Nicosia, Cyprus, claims that Johanna Beispielacker is owed a €612.00 refund from energy bills for 2023–2025, but demands a one-time "processing fee" of €49.90 be transferred by 27 November 2026 to a Cypriot IBAN before the refund is paid out.
data.explanation: This letter has strong hallmarks of an advance-fee scam: it asks you to pay money upfront to receive a much larger sum, uses a foreign (Cypriot) bank account for a supposedly German consumer matter, and threatens that your "claim" expires if you miss a very short deadline. Genuine German authorities or utilities do not require an upfront fee to pay out a refund. Do not transfer any money. It is safer to verify the sender independently (e.g. via your actual energy provider or a consumer protection organisation such as the Verbraucherzentrale) and consider reporting the letter as a scam. If in doubt, seek advice from a consumer protection centre before acting.

warnings: This matches the classic advance-fee ("pay a fee to unlock a larger refund") scam pattern and should be treated with strong suspicion.
The payee IBAN (CY17 0020 0128 0000 0012 0052 7600) is in Cyprus, which is unusual and risky for a supposed German consumer/energy refund matter.
The sender pressures with a very short deadline and claims the refund will be forfeited permanently, a common scam tactic.
The sender's contact details use a generic example-style email domain and give no verifiable company registration or authority identifier.
Do not transfer money to the IBAN provided without independently verifying the sender through a trusted channel.
